paper.title: DoReMi: Grounding Language Model by Detecting and Recovering from Plan-Execution Misalignment
paper.central_claim: Using an LLM both to plan and to generate execution constraints, and a VLM to continuously detect constraint violations, lets robot arms and humanoids immediately detect and recover from plan-execution misalignment, giving higher task success and shorter completion time.
paper.scope_decision: in_scope: LLM planner plus LLM-authored constraints checked continuously by a VLM with abort-and-replan, controlling a simulated UR5 arm and simulated/real humanoid.

preliminary_judgment: Written after reading the fixed text, before opening this paper's seat records: system_method. Same LLM/VLM baselines and IM-Oracle; constraint vs frequency not isolated; FT confound. Expected online, scoped, measurement 2 under anchors v2, causality 2-3.

signatures.object: plan step + LLM-generated constraints checked continuously by a VLM binary detector during low-level skill execution
signatures.information: LLM sees instruction, previous skills and violation notes; VLM sees camera image and 'Is the constraint satisfied?' question; sim success by environment; IM-Oracle baseline gets oracle feedback
signatures.operation: LLM picks next skill (argmax over skills) and emits constraints; every 0.2 s BLIP-2 answers Yes/No per constraint; first violation aborts the skill and triggers replanning with violation text in the prompt
signatures.conditions: constraints expressible as visual Yes/No; detector accuracy adequate; synthetic disturbances (drop, noise, obstacles, pick failure)
signatures.feedback: VLM verdicts (learned, not ground truth) + LLM replanning
signatures.selection_rule_data: any False verdict -> abort and replan; no ensembling or confirmation
signatures.persistence: violation info appended to prompt within the episode
signatures.later_use: next planning call in the episode
signatures.claimed_effect: higher success and shorter time than SayCan/CLIPort/Inner Monologue
signatures.failure_boundary: complex scenes degrade zero-shot VLM (prepare-food 37-40%); constraint correctness unchecked

signatures.object: LoRA fine-tune of BLIP-2 on 128 image-text pairs (DoReMi-FT)
signatures.information: Small humanoid-scene dataset with fruit objects
signatures.operation: parameter-efficient fine-tune of the constraint detector
signatures.output: detector with higher TP/lower FN on humanoid tasks
signatures.conditions: single A100; evaluation tasks may overlap fine-tune scenes
signatures.claimed_effect: prepare-food success 37% -> 91% (sim); generalizes to unseen objects/backgrounds/tasks (qualitative)
signatures.failure_boundary: generalization shown qualitatively; overlap not controlled

gap.author_gap: Hierarchical LLM grounding assumes skills execute plans perfectly; feedback after each step is late and Inner Monologue needs manually designed queries and cannot run at high frequency.
gap.checked_gap: Real and specific (delayed feedback, ambiguous open-ended scene descriptions) and quantified against the nearest neighbour in the paper (IM, IM-Oracle). Execution-monitoring literature outside LLM planners is not discussed.

lineage_closest_adjacent.name: Inner Monologue (IM)
lineage_closest_adjacent.solved: success detectors and scene descriptors fed back to LLM after each step

gap.residue: VLM accuracy in complex scenes, correctness of LLM-generated constraints, real-world trial counts, latency and call cost.
gap.stakes: SayCan fails under disturbance; IM recovers late or not at all (e.g. 40-68% vs 90-95% with obstacle/drop disturbances).
gap.method_response: LLM writes task-specific constraints; VLM answers binary questions continuously; violation triggers replanning.
gap.remaining_gap: Complex-scene detector reliability, non-visual constraints, real trials and cost.
unresolved: Lineage beyond IM/SayCan/CLIPort not pinned locally.

assessment.evidence_level_reason: Closed-loop simulation with environment-judged success (20 s timeout) and counted episodes for Table I; real humanoid lacks trial counts; tasks, disturbances and fine-tune built on the same task families, so no transfer. Both seats agree.
assessment.author_claim_preserved: Using an LLM both to plan and to generate execution constraints, and a VLM to continuously detect constraint violations, lets robot arms and humanoids immediately detect and recover from plan-execution misalignment, giving higher task success and shorter completion time.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Under author-injected drops/noise/obstacles in simulation, planner-authored constraints with continuous BLIP-2 checking and abort-and-replan beat SayCan, CLIPort and Inner Monologue (same Vicuna-13B/BLIP-2) on success and execution time, approaching IM-Oracle success; prepare-food and real-humanoid gains depend on a fine-tuned detector not given to baselines and real results lack trial counts.
assessment.cannot_be_claimed: Framework-alone real-world gains; which of constraint specificity or polling frequency drives the effect; generality to other planners; calibrated detector reliability in complex scenes.
assessment.retained: not_applicable: static monitoring harness plus offline detector fine-tuning

G.reason: Both seats 3. Specific bottleneck (hierarchical LLM planners assume skills execute as planned; end-of-skill feedback is late and open-ended VLM descriptions are ambiguous) with the nearest neighbour (Inner Monologue) reimplemented and an oracle bound; execution-monitoring lineage outside LLM planners only sketched.

M.reason: Both seats 3. Reconstructable reasoning (planner-authored binary constraints reduce VLM ambiguity; continuous polling enables early abort) with distinguishable predictions (time below IM-Oracle at similar success); untested assumptions: generated constraints are correct, complete and visually decidable.

X.reason: Both seats 3. Algorithm 1, 0.2 s polling, abort-and-replan rule, models and an example trace are given; real loop at 1 Hz stated. Missing: full prompt p0, constraint-correctness checks, IM baseline details, Table II per-cell n, fine-tune split; the Appendix V-C example trace is itself internally inconsistent (agg:E003), so the printed pipeline example is not a faithful run log.

measurement.reason: Resolved toward sol (son55 3). Simulation success is environment-judged with a 20 s timeout, and Table I gives n = 4 seeds x 12 episodes with SD, plus a detector confusion audit for humanoid tasks. But Table II (humanoid simulation) states no episode counts (agg:E001) and the real humanoid results are bare percentages without trial counts. Anchors v2 refinement: criterion present but denominators incomplete (some tasks with counts, some without) -> 2.

causality.reason: Resolved toward son55 (sol 2). Same Vicuna-13B planner and BLIP-2 detector across SayCan, CLIPort, IM and zero-shot DoReMi; IM-Oracle separates feedback accuracy (DoReMi approaches oracle success) from immediacy (DoReMi faster than oracle); detector variants ablated. The headline zero-shot gains (Table I, humanoid obstacle/move-box) are therefore matched-model comparisons. Unseparated: constraint specificity vs polling frequency, single planner backbone, and - for prepare-food and both real tasks - the fine-tuned detector, which IM never receives (agg:E002; real zero-shot DoReMi equals IM at 20%). That confound narrows the real/prepare-food claims rather than the central sim claim, so 3, not 2.

holdout.reason: Both seats 2. Tasks and disturbances were authored for the method; the 128-pair fruit fine-tune set vs prepare-food evaluation overlap is uncontrolled; unseen-object/background/task generalisation is shown qualitatively (Fig. 6); no held-out planner.

statistics.reason: Both seats 3. Mean and SD over 4 seeds x 12 episodes (Table I), SD in Table II, success by disturbance level, detector TP/FN/FP/TN; no paired tests, and Table II/real n unstated keep it below 4.

cost.reason: Both seats 2. Execution time, sub-0.1 s detector query, 0.2 s polling and 1 Hz real loop reported, baselines share LLM/VLM; VLM query counts, LLM calls, failed-episode time and fine-tuning compute are not priced.

resolutions.reason: Anchors v2 binding refinement: success criterion present but denominators incomplete across tasks (Table II humanoid cells and real trials have none) caps at 2; the detector audit does not supply the missing outcome denominators.

shared_error_corrections.correction: The example trace is internally inconsistent: after detector feedback, step (5) picks the green block but step (6) places the red block, then (7) picks green again. It illustrates the format only and is not a faithful run log; Algorithm 1 remains the authoritative description.

shared_error_corrections.seats_value: Both seats treat the real-robot results as indicative DoReMi evidence (sol notes training dependence).
shared_error_corrections.correction: On Prepare-food-real zero-shot DoReMi equals IM (20 vs 20) and on Stack-real it is 20 vs 10; the 90/80% figures belong to DoReMi-FT, and IM was never given the fine-tuned detector. The real-world rows therefore support 'fine-tuned detector inside the DoReMi loop' rather than the framework alone.
